# The Foothills · Book II, pp. 144–149
# Generated by the extractor — fix the extractor, not this file.
PAGE	144
P	Two days northwest of Stonetop, the rolling <b>Flats</b> (page 126) give way to hills, climbing up into the <b>Whitefang Mountains</b> (page 480). The <b>Highway</b> (page 270) cuts through these hills, leading to <b>Barrier Pass</b> (page 26). To the east, the hills wrap around the <b>Great Wood</b> (page 200).
P	The Foothills are rugged and forest-strewn, crisscrossed with streams, dotted with gorges and ponds and small lakes. In ages past, it was a borderland between the <b>Rime</b> <b>Lords</b> (page 316) and the <b>Green Lords</b> (page 210), and later it was the extent of the <b>Barrow Builders'</b> reach (page 34).
P	Nowadays, it is mostly uninhabited, but both Stonetop and Barrier Pass come here to harvest timber.

HR
H3	Always
B	Hills rising up from the Flats, mountains looming behind them
B	Young thin trees on the southernmost slopes, getting bigger and older as you press into the hills
B	Echoes of birdsong, beast-bellows, tumbling rocks, raised voices

B	Muggy, humid heat
B	Sweat stinging your eyes as you hump up another slope
B	Cold clear water from a gurgling stream, tasting better than anything

H3	Autumn
B	Slopes turned red and orange and yellow, then black and brown and gray
B	Plump squirrels and other critters, busily foraging for winter
B	Cold, clammy mist lasting well into the day

B	Waist-deep snow drifts in the valleys
B	Frozen-over streams, water gurgling ominously from below
B	Squeak of trees, swaying in the cold wind
B	Short, magical twilight as the sun drops below the mountains

H2	Hooks
B	A logging expedition goes missing
B	Loggers stumble upon a ruin or corrupted site
B	Someone went missing on a logging trip years ago, and now they reappear
B	Heavy rains wash out a stretch of the Highway, blocking access to good timber
B	An adventurer claims to know the location of an old barrow in the Foothills, said to be laden with gold and other treasure
PAGE	146
H2	Logging trips
HR
P	A typical logging trip generates a wagonload of timber (Value 2), and requires:
C	A wagon and two horses;
C	~20 able-bodied workers; and
C	Pulling Together over 9-12 days (for travel and work)
P	Trips traditionally take place in autumn, after the harvest is complete and only if there are no more-pressing needs in town.
P	The <b>Palisade</b> steading improvement
P	requires ~1,000 logs of good timber (Value
P	3). A wagonload of timber (Value 2) contains ~40-50 logs, meaning you need
P	~20-25 wagonloads. To gather that much timber:
C	You need ~20 able-bodied workers, a wagon, and two horses working for the course of a season
C	You must talk to a few town elders, and get their support
C	You risk accidents and attacks
C	You must spend 1 Surplus (to feed and equip the loggers) and reduce Fortunes by 1 (because of so many people and resources being away for so long)
C	The steading must Pull Together over the course of the season
PAGE	147
TH	steading improvement
C	<b>PERMANENT</b>
P	<b>LOGGING CAMP</b>
P	Suppose we built a few cabins and kept loggers up there year-round?
P	Requires all of the following:
C	Two or three permanent dwellings, just off the Highway
C	Supplies, furnishings, and tools for those dwellings (Value 2)
C	5-6 capable adults, willing and able to relocate and log year-round
C	An extra wagon (Value 3) and extra horse or mule (Value 3) to haul timber to and from Stonetop
C	Four seasons of operation, each generating a wagonload of timber (Value 2)
P	When you <b><i>mark all the requirements</i></b>, add "Logging: timber, wood" to the resources list and increase Fortunes by 1.
P	Henceforth, as long as the camp is in operation, the steading has a ready supply of timber for improvements and other projects, and it consumes 1 less Surplus than usual in winter.
P	However, the logging camp consumes
P	1 Surplus every summer or else it ceases operation.

HR

P	4 Dense thicket/brush
P	5-6 Swath/copse of one type of tree
P	7-8 Gentle slope or valley
P	9 Steep slope: forested, overgrown
P	10 Sheer rock face, bluff, rocky outcrop
P	11 Clearing, meadow, burn site
P	12 Cave, cavern, grotto
P	If you like, roll 1d6 for size/scope/intensity.

HR

H2	Dangers
HR
H3	Hazards
B	Getting lost among the hills and trees
B	Treacherous terrain (loose footing, scree, slippery slopes, potholes, deadfall, etc.)
B	Flash flooding, especially in ravines and valleys
B	Harsh weather, especially rain and snow
B	Something tall to climb, and reason to climb it
B	<b>Hazardous growth</b> (page 219), from the time of the Green Lords
